messages:
Caroline: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we explicitly split policy evaluation into two orthogonal phases: hard constraints (region, tenant SLA, data residency) and soft objectives (latency/cost score).
Raj: What problem are we solving with that split?
Caroline: Two things: 1) make pre-filtering cheap so we avoid scoring incompatible routes, 2) let objective scoring be pluggable / experimental without touching constraint semantics.
Tess: Sounds good. Concern: how do we keep behavior deterministic during rollout? scoring changes could move traffic.
Mike: +1. Also want to avoid full recompile of adapters for every scoring tweak. We should expose a tiny stable contract for constraints so sidecars/libraries can short-circuit early.
Sam: Rollout plan idea: constraint schema is versioned and backward compatible; scoring is a separate service-level flag that can be toggled per-tenant. Canary scoring via shadow runs and compare deltas.
Olga: Can we get a compact proto/JSON example to make sure we mean the same thing?
Caroline: sure, sketch below (pseudo):
```
message PolicyEvalRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  RouteContext ctx = 2;
  repeated Constraint constraints = 3; // hard checks
  repeated Objective objectives = 4; // soft scoring inputs
}

message PolicyEvalResponse {
  repeated RouteCandidate allowed = 1; // passes hard constraints
  repeated ScoredRoute ranked = 2; // optional, produced by scoring phase
  enum ConstraintStatus { OK = 0; FAIL = 1; }
}
```
Raj: That makes sense. Implementation notes: constraint checks must be O(1)-ish (index lookups) — no network calls. scoring can call heuristics or parity services.
Tess: How do we signal why a route was rejected (for operator debugging)? We need reason codes in the response.
Mike: Add a small reason enum to allowed/denied with short strings. Keep size small.
Caroline: Good. Also thinking about eviction semantics: if a constraint changes (e.g., region allowed list), we need invalidation hooks for route caches.
Sam: Cache invalidation is tricky. Suggest TTL on constraint cache + explicit pub/sub for immediate invalidation in dedicated/private tenants. Hosted can tolerate short TTLs.
Olga: For adapters: keep the current adapter interface but add two optional callbacks: prefilter(constraints) -> candidates, and score(candidates, objectives) -> ranked. Old adapters default to combined eval.
Mike: That lets us roll scoring improvements behind flags without touching constraint codepath. Nice.
infra-bot: policy-sim job completed for tenant=acme at 2026-03-21T14:10Z :white_check_mark:
Caroline: Results from the sim look promising — average reroute churn <0.3% when scoring changes, but constraint deltas produced immediate rejections as expected.
Raj: Next steps?
Caroline: 1) Draft RFC with proto and adapter changes. 2) Small shim in router to call prefilter then optionally score. 3) Telemetry: record constraint hits/fails + score deltas per-tenant. 4) Migration plan (TTL + ps/invalidation).
Tess: Can I own the telemetry piece? I can add reason histograms to the per-route dashboards.
Tess: Also want an alert if constraint rejections for a tenant suddenly spike.
Sam: I'll write the migration checklist for Dedicated vs Hosted. Include how to force invalidation via console.
Olga: I'll prototype adapter shim this week.
Mike: I'll review the RFC and add adapter tests.
Caroline: Great—I'll open the RFC draft and ping reviewers. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
